messages:
maria: Quick postmortem follow-up from tonight's brief p99 spike during a throughput burst. We observed a recurring pattern tied to cache warmup after autoscale. Need owners, exact dates, and SLO/SLA amendment text.

ben: I'll take the cache-warmup investigation. Plan: reproduce in staging with replayed traffic and capture KV hit/miss heatmaps. ETA 8 business days.

ash: I'll own dashboard and customer SLO language. Suggest adding a short-term p99 target change for the impacted route and a throughput SLO per-shard while we stabilize.

maria: Proposed temporary SLO: p99 = 300ms (30-day rolling) for text-gen-public route, contingent on dashboards+rollback logic. Also propose an automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model if p99 > 500ms for 5m.

ben: Quick note on remediation timeline: short-term cache tuning PR in ~10 days, longer eviction-policy refactor in ~4 weeks. Need a dev GPU for profiling.

ops-bot: Ticket SRE-7001 created: "followup/cache-warmup-and-slo-amendment" with checklist template and placeholders for owners.

ash: Draft alert (5m eval) for p99 spike:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="text-gen-public"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.30
```
I'll add panels: per-shard p50/p90/p99, qps by shard, and a 7-day error-budget burn.

maria: Milestones to add to the ticket: dashboards+alerts in prod by 2002520000 (48h), cache PR opened by 2003200000 (10 days), eviction refactor PR by 2005200000 (28 days). Also add weekly 15m reviews for 3 weeks post-deploy.

ben: Added milestones and linked the replay notebook. Will request infra resources now.

ash: I'll draft temporary SLA blurb for legal: "Temporary SLO amendment: text-gen-public p99 target = 300ms (30-day rolling). This is a short-term change while we remediate cache warmup behavior; automatic rollback triggers defined in SRE-7001."

maria: Thanks. Final ask: each owner add explicit rollback criteria and the exact signal that constitutes an SLA violation into SRE-7001. I'll approve the temporary SLO once dashboards and rollback are in place. :thumbsup:
